name: How do I know if an interior wall is load-bearing or just a partition?

mainEntity.name: How do I know if an interior wall is load-bearing or just a partition?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can identify a load-bearing wall by checking attic rafters, ceiling joists, and foundation supports. Walls running perpendicular to ceiling joists or positioned directly above foundation beams or lower-level bearing walls usually carry weight. In contrast, non-load-bearing partition walls usually run parallel to joists above them. Before cutting into drywall or planning an open-concept layout, an on-site evaluation confirms whether a wall carries structural weight, roof loads, or second-story loads, preventing sag or catastrophic framing failure during demolition.
acceptedAnswer.description: Walls running perpendicular to ceiling joists or sitting directly over foundation beams are usually load-bearing. An on-site framing assessment confirms weight-bearing status.
